identification.summary: North Korean cyber espionage actor that Mandiant (then FireEye) named APT37 (Reaper) in February 2018. Mandiant says it is likely active since at least 2012 and focuses on public and private sectors primarily in South Korea, with 2017 expansion to Japan, Vietnam and the Middle East [S1]. The group has exploited zero-days in Adobe Flash and Internet Explorer [S1][S2][S4]. Recent reporting describes RokRAT delivered through LNK lures with cloud-service C2 [S6][S7], tools that reach air-gapped networks [S8], and a supply-chain compromise of a gaming platform used by ethnic Koreans in China [S9].
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant: likely active since at least 2012 [S1]. Kaspersky's Operation Daybreak, the earliest dated campaign in these sources, began in March 2016 [S2].
identification.notes: Mandiant believes APT37 aligns with activity publicly reported as ScarCruft (Kaspersky) and Group123 (Cisco Talos) [S1]. Volexity tracks it as InkySquid [S3] and AhnLab as RedEyes [S5]. Microsoft's public naming map (retrieved 2026-10-15) lists no Microsoft name with APT37, ScarCruft, Reaper or InkySquid as an alias, so no Microsoft name is assigned here [S11]. Zscaler coverage lists 'Ruby Sleet' as an APT37 alias, but Microsoft's map ties Ruby Sleet to CERIUM / VELVET CHOLLIMA; see gaps [S8][S11].

attribution.sponsor: Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) [S1][S4].
attribution.confidence: Mandiant: high confidence that the activity is carried out on behalf of the North Korean government [S1]. Google TAG describes APT37 as North Korean government-backed [S4]. Zscaler calls APT37 DPRK-backed [S8]. ESET calls ScarCruft North Korea-aligned [S9]. No US government attribution was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Malware development artifacts and targeting aligned with North Korean state interests (Mandiant) [S1]. Consistent tooling (RokRAT, BLUELIGHT) and a victim set of North Korea experts, defectors and North Korea-focused media across vendor reporting [S3][S5][S6][S7][S9].

objectives: Strategic intelligence collection on behalf of the North Korean state [S1]. Collection centers on South Korean policy circles, North Korea experts, defectors, journalists and human-rights activists; AhnLab describes the task as monitoring the lives of specific individuals [S5][S6][S7]. ESET assesses that refugees or defectors from the Yanbian region were the likely targets of the 2024-2026 supply-chain campaign [S9]. SentinelLabs assessed the group may seek threat research to learn whether defenders have detected its techniques [S6]. Mandiant notes access to wiper malware [S1].

sectors: Cybersecurity and threat intelligence professionals (assessed future target)
regions: Japan, Vietnam and the Middle East (2017) [S1]
Russia, Nepal, China, India, Kuwait and Romania (Operation Daybreak victims) [S2]
China: Yanbian region ethnic Korean community [S9]
targeting.notes: Industry sectors and the 2017 regional expansion come from Mandiant [S1]. Individual targeting comes from AhnLab, SentinelLabs, Seqrite and ESET [S5][S6][S7][S9]. The cybersecurity-professional target is SentinelLabs' forecast based on a Kimsuky report used as a decoy, not an observed campaign [S6].

capabilities.summary: Mandiant describes an expanding toolset including zero-day access and wiper malware [S1]. Kaspersky tied Flash zero-day CVE-2016-4171 to ScarCruft and reported that its Operation Erebus used CVE-2016-4117 and watering holes [S2]. In 2021 the group used Internet Explorer exploits (CVE-2020-1380, CVE-2021-26411) in a watering hole on Daily NK, delivering Cobalt Strike and the BLUELIGHT backdoor [S3]. In 2022 it exploited IE JScript zero-day CVE-2022-41128 through an Office document that loaded a remote RTF template [S4]. In 2023 AhnLab found FadeStealer (keylogging, screenshots, removable-media theft, audio wiretapping) delivered via CHM files, with a Go backdoor using the Ably platform for C2 [S5]. RokRAT is the recurring backdoor; recent chains use LNK files, fileless XOR-decoded payloads and C2 via Dropbox, pCloud and Yandex [S6][S7]. The 2025-26 Ruby Jumper toolset included RESTLEAF (Zoho WorkDrive C2), SNAKEDROPPER (installs a Ruby runtime), THUMBSBD and VIRUSTASK (removable-media relay and infection to reach air-gapped systems), plus FOOTWINE and BLUELIGHT [S8]. BirdCall, described as an evolution of RokRAT, has Windows and Android versions; the Android version collects contacts, SMS, call logs, documents, media and private keys and records audio [S9].

campaigns.name: Operation Daybreak
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky reported a ScarCruft campaign beginning in March 2016 that used Flash zero-day CVE-2016-4171 against high-profile victims in several countries.

campaigns.name: Expansion beyond the Korean peninsula
campaigns.summary: Mandiant reports APT37 expanded targeting to Japan, Vietnam and the Middle East and to industrial verticals.

campaigns.name: Flash zero-day CVE-2018-4878 / APT37 naming
campaigns.summary: Mandiant published its APT37 report after a February 2 blog on a Flash zero-day used by the group.

campaigns.name: Daily NK watering hole (InkySquid)
campaigns.summary: Volexity reported injected code on Daily NK exploiting IE CVE-2020-1380 and CVE-2021-26411 to deliver Cobalt Strike and BLUELIGHT.

campaigns.name: Itaewon-lure IE zero-day (CVE-2022-41128)
campaigns.summary: Google TAG reported Office documents themed on the Itaewon Halloween crowd crush exploiting an IE JScript zero-day against South Korean users; reported to Microsoft 2022-10-31 and patched 2022-11-08.

campaigns.name: FadeStealer wiretapping (RedEyes)
campaigns.summary: AhnLab reported CHM spear-phishing delivering FadeStealer and a Go backdoor with Ably C2 against defectors, activists and professors.

campaigns.name: Targeting of North Korea experts and media; Kimsuky-report decoy testing
campaigns.summary: SentinelLabs reported RokRAT phishing against media and North Korea experts and malware testing that used a Kimsuky report as a decoy.

campaigns.name: Operation HanKook Phantom
campaigns.summary: Seqrite reported LNK-based phishing against people tied to the National Intelligence Research Association, using a fake newsletter and a Kim Yo Jong statement as lures to deliver RokRAT.

campaigns.name: Ruby Jumper (air-gapped networks)
campaigns.summary: Zscaler ThreatLabz reported LNK lures and new tools using Zoho WorkDrive C2 and removable media to bridge air-gapped systems.

campaigns.name: Yanbian gaming platform supply-chain compromise
campaigns.summary: ESET reported trojanized Windows updates (RokRAT then BirdCall) and Android BirdCall on a Yanbian-themed gaming platform (sqgame per coverage), probably active since late 2024.

diamond.capability: Zero-day and n-day exploits (Flash, IE), RokRAT, BLUELIGHT, FadeStealer, BirdCall (Windows and Android), and air-gap tooling (THUMBSBD, VIRUSTASK) [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S8][S9].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised news sites as watering holes [S3]; commercial cloud and messaging services for C2, including Ably, Dropbox, pCloud, Yandex and Zoho WorkDrive [S5][S7][S8]; a legitimate software-update channel for supply-chain delivery [S9].
diamond.victim: South Korean academics, former officials and North Korea-focused media; defectors, activists and professors; ethnic Koreans in Yanbian, China; 2017 industrial targets in Japan, Vietnam and the Middle East [S1][S5][S6][S7][S9].
diamond.socioPolitical: Regime-security intelligence on defectors, critics and South Korean policy toward North Korea [S5][S6][S9].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints with legacy IE components invoked through Office, LNK and CHM handling, removable media crossing air gaps, and Android devices [S4][S5][S8][S9].

gaps: No Microsoft name confirmed. Microsoft's public mapping has no APT37/ScarCruft alias; Zscaler and other third-party alias lists cite 'Ruby Sleet' (and one list 'Opal Sleet'), which Microsoft maps to CERIUM and to APT43/Konni respectively. Treat these as unverified [S8][S11].
No US government (CISA/FBI/DOJ) attribution document specific to APT37 was located.
Primary reports from Volexity, Seqrite, Zscaler and SentinelLabs were read only through search summaries or secondary coverage. The full Mandiant PDF was not reviewed.

Kaspersky's 2019 Bluetooth device-harvester report (securelist.com/scarcruft-continues-to-evolve-introduces-bluetooth-harvester/90729/, in the imported references) was not reviewed in this pass and is excluded from the timeline.
Overlap with Kimsuky (APT43) is not assessed here; the clusters are tracked separately.
Victim counts for the Daily NK watering hole and the Yanbian supply-chain campaign are not public in the sources gathered [S3][S9].

Imported aliases 'Venus 121', 'APT-C-28', 'ATK4', 'Operation Erebus' as an alias, and 'Moldy Pisces' were not confirmed by a cited source in this pass; Operation Erebus is a Kaspersky campaign name, not a group alias [S2].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (environment): Key terrain includes email of Korea-policy staff, academics and liaison personnel, South Korean partner endpoints, and removable media used to move data across air gaps [S1][S7][S8]. STEP 2 (effects): C2 over commercial cloud services (Dropbox, pCloud, Yandex, Zoho WorkDrive, Ably) blends with legitimate traffic and weakens perimeter detection [S5][S7][S8]. STEP 3 (adversary model): Topical lure (news event, think-tank newsletter, official statement) then LNK, CHM or weaponized document, then fileless RokRAT or similar with cloud C2, then collection including keystrokes and audio [S4][S5][S6][S7][S8]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is continued spear-phishing of South Korean and allied Korea specialists timed to peninsula news events [S4][S7]. MDCOA is use of removable-media tooling to reach air-gapped partner or mission networks, or a trusted update channel for supply-chain access, as already shown against civilian targets [S8][S9]. Candidate indicators: LNK or CHM attachments with Korean-language decoys; Office documents fetching remote RTF templates; non-browser processes calling cloud-storage APIs; unexpected Ruby runtime installs; LNK files replacing documents on USB drives [S4][S5][S7][S8].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track lure themes tied to Korean peninsula events and warn Korea-focused staff, since APT37 used the Itaewon disaster as a lure within days [S4]. (2) Authorities: activity largely targets ROK persons and networks; response affecting partner networks requires coordination through USFK and ROK channels rather than unilateral DODIN actions. (3) Mission assurance: removable-media controls on air-gapped enclaves directly counter THUMBSBD and VIRUSTASK-style tooling [S8]. (4) Coordination: share cloud-service C2 indicators with providers and with DC3 and the DIB CS program, since the infrastructure is commercial [S7][S8].
